item.title: From consumer wearable hypertension signals to clinical diagnosis, mind the gap
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, Wise’s report on Apple Watch hypertension notifications highlights a familiar tension in preventive care: increasing opportunities for detection while risking false reassurance and avoidable workload when the test is not designed to rule disease out (1). item.title: Why some patients may feel safer with AI than with clinicians
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear EDitor The BMJ article rightly highlights that AI-assisted disclosure may support earlier detection and shared decision making, particularly when patients feel unable to verbalise distressing material in time-pressured, high-stakes consultations. It also points to an uncomfortable reality - anonymity and the absence of judgement can feel safer than clinical encounters. item.title: Re: Cancer is a chronic disease: why don’t we treat it as one?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor We were delighted to see Adam et al [1] arguing that cancer survivorship care should be part of routine chronic disease management in primary care. Survivors of bone and soft tissue sarcoma have a chronic disease state. Many have been treated as children and most have had surgery for tumour removal. Some have had amputations. item.title: Vitamin D supplementation before IVF in PCOS: limited effect despite severe deficiency — implications for high-risk populations
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor The recent multicentre, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial by Zhang et al. evaluated vitamin D supplementation prior to in vitro fertilisation (IVF) in women with polycystic ovary syndrome (PCOS). item.title: Re: Wes Streeting’s links to private health and tech companies under fire in wake of Mandelson texts
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor, 'Streeting said the donation was “towards staffing costs in my constituency office.”' He should be expected to provide a breakdown; this sounds like a universal get-out-of-jail-card. More transparency is needed: after all, we cannot accept as little as a Post-It note, some of which would have been very acceptable in my Secretary's office... item.title: Re: Ultrasound should be the first line investigation for Osgood-Schlatter's disease with use of x-ray outdated.
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor X-ray is an outdated and unnecessary investigation for Osgood Schlatter’s or other growth related, traction apophyseal complaints such as Sever’s or Sinding-Larsen-Johansson. item.title: England left behind on effective alcohol policy
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor As reported in The BMJ, Wales will increase its minimum unit pricing (MUP) of alcohol from £0.50 per unit to £0.65 from October.[1] This follows the same evidence-based step that Scotland has taken in increasing its MUP to ensure the policy’s effectiveness is not eroded by inflation. item.title: Re: Medical schools: What’s happening with the planned expansion of places in England?
item.description: Agreement: I AgreeBody: Dear Editor Alison's piece is revealing and should be more widely made known, in my view. I recall many such commitments over the years, only some of which were ever implemented. There were several that recommended only small increases, and one - Willink, I think - that proposed a reduction in medical school intake.
